ONE IDEA → SCRIPT + SHOT LIST + CAPTION
Editorial sample for this guide, not a recorded Kimi session.
Your Kimi output will vary. Adjust timing after reading the script aloud.

THE BRIEF
Idea: Three phone shots that make a small desk look good on camera.
Audience: Creators filming at home with a phone.
Next step: Save this and try the sequence before their next Reel.
Tone: Conversational and practical.
Location and props: Desk, phone, notebook, pen, stable phone support.
Verified product claims: None.

01 / SCRIPT
Format: 30-second vertical Reel. 71 spoken words.

0–5s / HOOK
Voiceover: “Filming at a small desk? Try three simple shots for your next Reel.”
On-screen text: “Small desk. Three simple shots.”

5–25s / THREE-BEAT WALKTHROUGH
Voiceover: “First, put your phone above the desk and frame just your hands.
Then move closer. Capture one detail: a pen, a key, a notebook.
Finally, turn the camera toward you and explain what you’re doing.
Cut between the wide view, the detail, and your face.”
On-screen text: “1. Overhead / 2. Detail / 3. Face to camera”

25–30s / NEXT STEP
Voiceover: “Save this and try the sequence before filming your next Reel.”
On-screen text: “Save it. Try it on your next Reel.”

02 / SHOT LIST

SHOT 1 / 0–5s
Line: “Filming at a small desk? Try three simple shots for your next Reel.”
Framing: Medium face-to-camera, phone static at eye level.
Action: Introduce the idea while sitting at the desk.
Text: “Small desk. Three simple shots.”

SHOT 2 / 5–10s
Line: “First, put your phone above the desk and frame just your hands.”
Framing: Static overhead using a stable support.
Action: Open the notebook and write one short line.
Text: “1. Overhead”

SHOT 3 / 10–15s
Line: “Then move closer. Capture one detail: a pen, a key, a notebook.”
Framing: Close detail, phone held steady or supported.
Action: Record the pen touching the page. Use window light.
Text: “2. Detail”

SHOT 4 / 15–20s
Line: “Finally, turn the camera toward you and explain what you’re doing.”
Framing: Medium face-to-camera, same setup as shot 1.
Action: Explain the action shown in shots 2 and 3.
Text: “3. Face to camera”

SHOT 5 / 20–25s
Line: “Cut between the wide view, the detail, and your face.”
Framing: A steady wide desk view; reuse the other framings in the edit.
Action: Close the notebook, then lift it slightly into frame.
Text: “Wide → detail → face”

SHOT 6 / 25–30s
Line: “Save this and try the sequence before filming your next Reel.”
Framing: Face-to-camera, same static phone position.
Action: Deliver the next step, then hold the final frame briefly.
Text: “Save it. Try it.”

FILMING NOTES
Film all face-to-camera lines together. Then capture the desk and detail
shots. Record narration separately if that is easier. If you lack a stable
overhead support, substitute a high-angle handheld view of one hand writing.
Do not balance the phone on an unstable object. Timings total 30 seconds;
read aloud and trim the wording if your natural delivery needs more time.

03 / CAPTION

Your next Reel can start right at your desk.

Pick one action worth showing, then film it three ways: an overhead view,
a close detail, and a quick face-to-camera explanation. Keep the background
simple and use the same light for each shot.

You now have a small sequence to cut between when you edit, instead of
one long take.

Save this and try the sequence before filming your next Reel.
